patch_description: The current algorithm sends every partition over a single Dijkstra shortest path, causing redundant transfers over the same (possibly expensive) links and ignoring parallel network paths. A better strategy is to (1) enumerate multiple candidate paths per destination (k-shortest simple paths by cost), (2) split the partitions across those parallel paths proportionally to their achievable throughput so load is balanced across networks, and (3) prefer the set of paths that minimizes the weighted sum of per-GB cost. This reduces redundant transfers over the same links, exploits multi-network topologies, and lowers total cost while keeping the BroadCastTopology structure intact (each partition gets exactly one path with its edge list). Edges missing cost data are given a large penalty so they are only used when necessary, and cached edge data is passed directly into the topology to avoid recomputation.
